life_summary: Franklin D. Richards (1821–1899) was an early LDS Church apostle who lived during the formative and expansion periods of the Church. Limited biographical information is available from standard sources, though he was the father of George F. Richards, who also became an apostle, and grandfather of LeGrand Richards. This three-generation succession of Richards family members in the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles represents one of the most remarkable family legacies in LDS Church history. His son George became the only person to serve as both Presiding Patriarch and President of the Quorum of the Twelve.
church_summary: Franklin D. Richards was called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and served in that capacity during the mid-to-late nineteenth century. He died in 1899. His apostolic service occurred during a transformative period in Church history, and his family's continued prominence in leadership—with his son George and grandson LeGrand both achieving high positions—demonstrates the Richards family's enduring influence on institutional development. Limited details about his specific assignments and teachings are readily available in modern sources.
